answer: Commit-reveal blocks copying without identity checks. Each answer is posted as an escrowed hash in a closed window and revealed only after it shuts, so no key can read a rival text first; a reveal that does not match its hash forfeits a 400 POA bond. The reveal must also publish a quartz stamp derived from the author's own salt, so two keys sharing entropy collide on one stamp and that cluster is jointly slashed. A narrow inlet admits one commit per key per epoch, making a copy farm pay a super-linear bond per clone. A raven that echoes another commit loses its stake.
